title: Norfolk Island Pine: Old Araucarias You Can Visit
meta_description: The whole species comes from one Pacific island eight kilometres long. Five araucarias mapped, including six in a ring around a Setubal fountain.
intro: The entire species comes from one Pacific island eight kilometres long, and it now stands over port cities from Hobart to the Atlantic coast of Portugal. Araucaria heterophylla grows in regular tiers, a candelabra of horizontal branches on a dead straight stem, which is why it reads as a tree drawn by a child and why nineteenth century gardeners could not resist it. Height is usually the point. The Malaga specimen, around 200 years old, is the tallest in its province; Barcelona's clears 27 metres above one of the most densely built neighbourhoods in Europe; Sintra's is the tallest tree at Monserrate. Setubal has six of them at 26 metres, standing in a ring around one old circular stone tank with a fountain in the middle. Hobart's is the one nearest home, and a local nurseryman asked in 2025 to name his favourite tree in the city picked it.
